t.E473.agn: In 2023 EFSA cited a group ADI of 40 mg/kg body weight for E473 and E474; it reported that in estimates based on current use levels, exposure exceeded this value in many age groups. Because E473 is not used in foods for infants below 16 weeks of age, no separate evaluation was made for this group.
t.E473.body: Sucrose esters are largely split during digestion into sugar (sucrose) and fatty acids.
t.E473.eff.0.t: The daily limit may be exceeded at current use levels
t.E473.eval: The fatty acid source may be vegetable or animal (including beef/pork); the source is often not stated on the label.
t.E473.prod: It is an emulsifier produced by esterifying sucrose with fatty acid esters or by extraction from sucroglycerides.
t.E473.regx.0: Re-evaluated (follow-up opinion); group ADI of 40 mg/kg body weight, estimated exposure exceeds the ADI in many age groups.
t.E473.summary: An emulsifier produced from sugar and fatty acids. It is used in cake, ice cream and cream-like products, and also in coatings for fruit.
t.E473.what: It is an emulsifier that allows oil and water to mix; it adjusts texture and consistency.
